req.title: Redirect count boundary
req.statement: The system shall accept /redirect/<n> with n in the range 1..30 inclusive and reject values above.

doc.reasoning: The requirement states /redirect/<n> must accept n in [1..30] inclusive and reject values above 30. The source code shows `redirect_n_times` uses `assert n > 0` (so n=0 triggers AssertionError/500) and the Flask route uses `<int:n>`. The upper bound of 30 must be enforced — examining the source, values above 30 should return 404 (httpbin enforces this via a URL converter or assertion). We need: EP tests for mid-range valid values, BVA tests at n=1, n=30, n=31, n=0, and NEG tests for out-of-range values. Each test uses Flask test_client with follow_redirects=True to reach the final 200, or checks redirect status without following. We assert exact status codes to catch comparison-operator mutations.

from httpbin.core import app
client = app.test_client()

def test_redirect_n1_lower_boundary_accepted():
    r = client.get('/redirect/1', follow_redirects=True)
    assert r.status_code == 200
    data = r.get_json()
    assert data is not None
    assert 'url' in data

test_redirect_n1_lower_boundary_accepted()

tests.name: test_redirect_decision_table_valid_vs_invalid
actions: GET /redirect/0 (invalid, below lower bound) -> expect non-2xx non-3xx
trace: R-HTTPBIN-048: Decision table covering all four boundary partitions in one test
tests.executable:
from httpbin.core import app
client = app.test_client()

def test_redirect_decision_table_valid_vs_invalid():
    r1 = client.get('/redirect/1', follow_redirects=False)
    assert r1.status_code == 302
    r30 = client.get('/redirect/30', follow_redirects=False)
    assert r30.status_code == 302
    r31 = client.get('/redirect/31', follow_redirects=False)
    assert r31.status_code >= 400
    assert r31.status_code < 500
    r0 = client.get('/redirect/0', follow_redirects=False)
    assert r0.status_code < 200 or r0.status_code >= 400

test_redirect_decision_table_valid_vs_invalid()
